title: NDPS special courts - how trial timelines actually work
p1:
A case under the NDPS Act does not move at the speed many people expect.

Many assume that a “special court” means a faster trial with a fixed deadline. The reality is more complex.
p2:
Special courts are created to handle NDPS cases with focused attention, but they do not automatically finish every trial quickly.

The timeline depends on several steps: investigation, filing of charges, examination of witnesses, evidence collection, and court hearings. A delay at any stage can extend the process.
p3:
One lesser-known point: the law may prioritize these cases, but prioritization is not the same as instant resolution. The court still has to follow procedures that protect both the prosecution and the accused.

The practical takeaway is that a special court changes the process structure, not a guaranteed end date. Knowing this helps set realistic expectations about how NDPS trials actually progress.
conclusion: Did you know that a special court does not always mean a quick trial? What part of NDPS trial timelines surprised you the most?
